name: trowel
description: Cat's-tongue trowel 140 x 65 mm, polished steel blade with a lacquered wooden handle (Hornbach article 6642994)

frame.origin: centre of volume, which lies in the handle; the blade's underside is the plane z = -0.0475 m
frame.z: normal of the blade, pointing up towards the handle when the tool lies blade down
frame.x: along the blade from the heel edge towards the tip

symmetry.mirror: the x-z plane; a mirror image is not a pose, so nothing is ambiguous for the pose estimator

source.kind: generated from calliper measurements and three photos of the real tool; no downloaded geometry
source.material: polished steel blade, steel rod and ferrule, lacquered beech handle

assumed.handle_profile: smooth curve through the five measured stations
assumed.from: a side photo of the tool (not included): the ferrule's axis sits 30 mm above the blade and 13 mm in front of the heel edge, and the handle leans 21 deg

to_verify: ferrule: horizontal distance from the heel edge to the top of its front rim (expected about 9 mm towards the tip) and the height of its centre (expected 30 mm)
heel corner rounding and tang shape, by eye against reference photos (not included)
mass on a scale (about the value printed by the build)
centre_of_mass_from: the parts of the mesh build weighted by material: steel at 7.85 g/cm3 for the blade, tang, rod, a 0.7 mm ferrule tube and a 5 mm tang assumed 60 mm into the handle; beech at 0.72 g/cm3 for the handle. That is 7 mm in front of the heel edge and 26 mm above the table, under the ferrule; the build's own estimate with a solid steel ferrule moves it 1.3 mm. The centre of volume, in the handle, is 42 mm behind it. Estimated mass 128 g, not weighed.
